I will keep my land in the usual wheat-maize cycle, because in Quzhou County that is the safest way for me to get grain from the same fields twice in one year. I will finish this winter wheat crop first, since it is already in the ground from last autumn, and then I will plant summer maize right after harvest. I would rather stay with a simple plan I can manage well than spread myself across too many crops. I will use improved seed for wheat and hybrid seed for maize because I want stable yield and stronger performance. I will fertilize enough to support grain filling but not push it too hard, because fertilizer costs money and too much nitrogen can cause problems. I will irrigate wheat more times than maize, since wheat in my area depends more on timely water in spring, while maize can often manage with summer rain plus a smaller number of irrigations if needed. I will use rotary tillage after harvest because it is practical and common for quick turnover between crops. I will spray pesticides only when needed for the main disease and insect pressure, because I want to protect yield without wasting money.
